draft.title: The Boston Tea Party and the Coercive Acts
card: In December 1773, colonists in Boston boarded ships of the East India Company and threw chests of taxed tea into the harbour. They were protesting the tax on tea and the Tea Act.
Britain saw the destruction of property as lawless defiance. In 1774 Parliament passed the Coercive Acts to punish Massachusetts and restore order.
One of these laws closed Boston's port until the tea was paid for. Others reduced self-government in Massachusetts, which had elected its own leaders until then.
Colonists called these laws the Intolerable Acts. Many in other colonies saw the punishment as a threat to their own rights, so resistance spread beyond Massachusetts.
draft.remember: Colonists destroyed tea, Britain punished Massachusetts, and the punishment pushed other colonies towards resistance.

a.q: Why did the Coercive Acts make colonists in other colonies more willing to resist Britain?
opts: They feared the same punishment could be used on them
They had already been told to pay for the destroyed tea
They were pleased that Britain had restored order in Boston
They had all taken part in the destruction of the tea
a.why: The Acts cut self-government and closed a port in one colony, so others feared their own rights were at risk. It is wrong to say they all took part: the tea was destroyed in Boston, and the Acts were a response to it.
a.clue: Think about what the punishment suggested for colonies not yet punished.

b.q: Daniel lives in a Virginia town in 1774 and did not join the Boston protest. He reads that Britain has closed Boston's port and cut Massachusetts self-government. Which view fits a colonist like Daniel?
opts: Britain's response to one colony threatens colonial rights
Boston's actions were lawful, so the Acts are fair
Closing one port will not affect any other colony
The Acts show Britain wants to lower taxes on tea
b.why: Daniel sees that Britain was willing to remove self-government, which colonies had long enjoyed, so his own colony could be next. The idea that the Acts were fair does not fit a colonist who called them Intolerable, and the Acts punished Massachusetts rather than cutting taxes.
b.clue: Ask what Britain's punishment of one colony might mean for the others.

a.best: They feared the same punishment could be used on them

b.best: Britain's response to one colony threatens colonial rights

problems.detail: The ships boarded in Boston (Dartmouth, Eleanor, Beaver) were not East India Company ships. They were privately owned vessels carrying the Company's tea. It should say 'ships carrying East India Company tea'.

'Massachusetts, which had elected its own leaders until then' overstates it. Under the 1691 charter the governor was already appointed by the Crown. The Massachusetts Government Act made the council appointed instead of elected and restricted town meetings, so the card should say something like 'had elected its council and run its own town meetings'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer each. The card has two factual slips: the tea ships were not East India Company ships, and Massachusetts did not elect all its own leaders before 1774, since its governor was already Crown-appointed.
